description: Diversity, Equity and Inclusion Advisory Committee proposes 2025 work plan.
Committee recommends $300,000 budget adjustment for lift station upgrades.
Funding will come from Wastewater Treatment Capital Reserve.
Saskatoon will join provincial recycling program by January 2028.
This aims to reduce current recycling utility fees.
City will explore joining the program earlier.

chips.text: Councillor Donauer supports province taking over recycling, reducing city services.
Saskatoon residents may see reduced recycling utility fees.
Exact financial impact on city and current providers remains unknown.
Administration will bring a financial strategy report this fall.

description: Committee recommends approving SaskEnergy agreement for Silverspring regulator station.
The agreement covers Parcel A in Section 12.
Committee recommends $106,250 bonus payment to SREDA.
Committee recommends approving SREDA's 2025 performance targets.
Committee recommends approving 2025 business tax abatements.
SREDA determines these incentive abatements.

chips.text: Businesses receiving SREDA incentives will get 2025 tax abatements.

description: City will appoint Mayor Block as proxy for Art Gallery AGM.
Councillors Dubois or Ford will serve if Mayor is absent.
Art Gallery of Saskatchewan Inc. AGM is April 29, 2025.

chips.text: City of Saskatoon is a member of The Art Gallery of Saskatchewan Inc.

description: Committee recommends enhancing 2025 Civic Survey demographic reporting.
Enhanced reporting will better reflect Saskatoon's diverse community.
Enhanced reporting will also provide more detailed ward reports.
Sets non-residential to residential tax ratio at 1.71.
Maintains 68% residential, 32% non-residential tax split.

chips.text: Councillor Donauer moved to refer the Chamber's letter for stakeholder engagement.
Non-residential property owners are affected by the tax ratio change.
Chamber of Commerce letter referred for stakeholder and resident engagement.

description: Committee recommends applying for federal transit funding.
This funding supports Saskatoon's five-year capital plan.

chips.text: Transit users could benefit from future capital improvements.

description: Brenda Southam, Sutherland Business Improvement District, recommended for Municipal Heritage Advisory Committee.
Appointment would be effective immediately.
Recommends three new members for Public Art Advisory Committee.
Appointments would serve until the end of 2026.

chips.text: Christie Keller, Whitney Robson, Luka Garden-Stringer recommended for committee.
Appointments include representatives for First Nations/Métis and youth communities.

description: Committee recommends Darren Doepker, Edward Agbai for 2025 Board of Revision.
June Gawdun proposed for Accessibility Advisory Committee.
Saskatoon Council on Aging director would represent agency.
Appointment would run until the end of 2026.

chips.text: Seniors and people with disabilities in Saskatoon.

description: Committee recommends Kelleher, Ford to Homelessness Subcommittee.
Committee recommends Mayor replace Pearce as Housing Lead.
City representative to vote for Andrew Denton.
Appointment to Remai Modern board of directors.
Term would expire after 2027 Annual General Meeting.
City applies for provincial funding to remediate 1202 19th Street West.
Site could be developed for housing insecure individuals and social needs.

chips.text: Councillor Timone raised concerns about ongoing illegal dumping and encampments at the site.
Rotary Community Garden Group's future use of the site is uncertain due to development.
Timeline for provincial funding application approval remains unknown.
Site is contaminated with hydrocarbons and metal impacts, limiting development.

description: Funds Discover Saskatoon $350,000 for a 2027 national sporting event.
Funding is conditional on winning the event bid.

chips.text: Mayor Block noted events attract visitors, residents, and help lower property tax pressure.
Saskatoon residents, local businesses, and hotel partners are affected.
Discover Saskatoon's CEO spoke in strong support of the funding request.

speakers.name: Steph Clovechok
speakers.summary: Steph Clovechok spoke in support of the application on behalf of Discover Saskatoon and Destination Hotels group.
said: Requests $350,000 for a confidential national winter sport event.
Event projects $15.7M economic impact, $1.7M provincial tax revenue.
Hosting brings pride, national attention, and long-term community benefits.

description: Introduces four bylaws for 2025 property tax and BID levies.
These bylaws are required for property tax billing in May.
One property tax bylaw uses a 1.71 assessment ratio.

chips.text: Councillor MacDonald declared a conflict of interest as a 33rd Street BID business owner.

description: Amends animal control bylaw to prohibit non-dogs in off-leash areas.
Requires accurate animal license information.
Does not limit household pet numbers.

chips.text: City Solicitor clarified zoning bylaw prohibits animal breeding operations in residential districts.
Kelsey Stroeder urged council to implement household pet limits and breeder licensing.
Administration offered to research pet limits for 2026-2027 budget if council directs.

speakers.name: Kelsey Stroeder
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: Animal Control Bylaw - CK 151-15
said: A dog crisis exists; Saskatoon needs pet limits and breeder regulations.
Regina's zoning bylaws prevent breeders/rescues in residential homes.
Breeders should be licensed; 10-12 pets per household is reasonable.

description: Amends traffic bylaw to permit shared e-scooters on public ways.

chips.text: Council had no further questions or debate on the proposed bylaw.
Competitive process required for up to two e-scooter vendors.

description: Sets 1.71 non-residential to residential tax ratio for 2025-2029.
This maintains 68% residential, 32% non-residential tax split.
